policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: The readings differ only in the conjunctive waw on the preposition (qere ועד vs ketiv עד). ASV renders the idiom מכף רגלו ועד קדקדו as 'from the sole of his foot unto his crown', where English supplies no 'and' for the waw in a from...unto pair, so the wording is identical under either reading. No ASV note is mapped to this unit; base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
